contract.reader: An engineer who has the series' z-transform and DFT background and must turn a pass/stop specification into filter coefficients that run on real hardware
contract.problem: Choosing between FIR and IIR, computing coefficients that meet a stated tolerance scheme, and implementing them without finite word length breaking the filter
contract.outcome: Specify a filter, design a linear-phase FIR filter by the window method (Hamming, Kaiser), design a Butterworth IIR filter by the bilinear transform with prewarping, compare the two, and choose structures and word lengths (second-order sections, scaling, saturation) that keep the result stable
contract.contribution: One running specification designed both ways and then quantized, with each claim (orders, attenuations, pole radii, noise gains, limit cycle) reproduced by four runnable scripts
contract.evidence: Derivations; four Python scripts with real output; window table measured for the entry; Kaiser's formulas; IEEE Std 754-2019, Oppenheim and Schafer (2010), Parks and McClellan (1972), Proakis and Manolakis (2007)
contract.limitations: No Parks-McClellan, Chebyshev or elliptic design computed; no frequency-response plot of the designs; fixed-point effects shown for one design

findings.location: Section 2.2 linear-phase equation (desktop-light-04; mobile-light-07); Section 3.4 Kaiser formulas (desktop-light-08; mobile-light-15); Section 4.3 coefficient arrays (desktop-light-12)
findings.problem: At 1280 px the 2.2 equation is cut before '= e^(-jωM/2) A(ω)', so A(ω) is used but never shown defined; the 3.4 display shows only 'M' of the order formula M = (A - 8)/(2.285 Δω), which the next paragraph and Exercise 1 use; the 4.3 'a' array is cut. Worse at 360 px; no scroll cue.
findings.whyItMatters: These are the definition the linear-phase argument rests on and the order estimate the Kaiser design depends on; a reader who misses the hidden scroll meets an undefined symbol and a missing formula.
findings.action: Break the 2.2 equation over two lines (aligned, with '= e^(-jωM/2) A(ω)' on its own line); set Kaiser's order formula as a separate display; put the two 4.3 arrays on separate lines.
findings.acceptance: On new captures the full 2.2 equation, both Kaiser formulas and both 4.3 arrays are visible without sideways scrolling at 1280 px, and at 360 px no line of the 2.2 equation or the order formula is cut.

findings.problem: The Hamming, Kaiser and Butterworth designs are reported only as worst-case numbers; no response is plotted against the tolerance scheme, although the scripts compute it.
findings.whyItMatters: A plot would show the trade-offs the text describes (unused passband margin of fixed windows, equal ripple, monotone Butterworth roll-off) instead of leaving them to inference.
findings.action: Add one generated figure: magnitude in dB, 0 to 500 Hz, of the three designs with the specification mask, data from the article's scripts, with a caption saying what to notice.
findings.acceptance: On new captures the figure appears in Section 3 or 4.5, legible at 1280 and 360 px and in dark mode, with all three curves inside the mask at 100 and 150 Hz.
